questions.q: What is normalization trying to accomplish?
options: Structuring tables to avoid storing the same fact in more than one place, and avoid cramming more than one fact into a single column
Making every table have exactly the same number of columns
Removing all foreign keys from a schema
Converting every table into a view
questions.explain: Normalization is a set of formal rules aimed at reducing duplication and column overload.

questions.q: What are the three rules that define First Normal Form (1NF)?
options: Every column holds a single atomic value, every row is unique with a primary key, and there are no repeating column groups
Every table must have exactly one column
Every column must be nullable
Every table must have a foreign key to every other table
questions.explain: These three rules together define the ground-floor requirement of 1NF.

questions.q: Why does storing multiple phone numbers as a comma-separated string in one column violate 1NF?
options: The column no longer holds a single atomic value — it crams a list into one field, making it unsearchable and unindexable
Comma-separated strings are not valid NVARCHAR data
It violates a UNIQUE constraint automatically
SQL Server physically cannot store commas in a column
questions.explain: A crammed-together value breaks atomicity, the first rule of 1NF, making simple searches require string parsing.

questions.q: How does AdventureWorks2012's Person.PersonPhone table demonstrate the fix for a 1NF violation?
options: It gives each phone number its own row, instead of cramming multiple numbers into one column on Person
It stores every phone number as a single JSON blob
It removes phone numbers from the database entirely
It requires every person to have exactly one phone number
questions.explain: One person can have many PersonPhone rows, each holding one atomic phone number — a one-to-many fix for the repeating-group problem.

questions.q: What relationship shape from Lessons 99-101 is PersonPhone's design an example of?
options: One-to-many — one Person can have many PersonPhone rows
One-to-one — exactly one phone number per person
Many-to-many via a junction table with no direct FK
No relationship — PersonPhone stands completely alone
questions.explain: PersonPhone.BusinessEntityID is an ordinary foreign key back to Person, allowing many phone rows per person.
